primary_justification: Source-reconciliation evidence shows three source-only blocker rows for Align Precision Group, Centric Brands, and Visual Edge Technology, but the raw current-period source evidence identifies these as collapsed_duplicate_dimension_path issuer-level rows with no output fair value, while related instrument-level rows carry the investable tranche detail. Adding the issuer wrapper rows as unified positions would duplicate child dimension paths rather than repair a missing production position.
patch_summary: No patch proposed. The residual is explained by duplicate-dimension issuer wrapper rows rather than a bounded parser miss suitable for adding unified holdings.
source_reconciliation_effect: No source-reconciliation patch expected. The blocker should remain subject to duplicate-dimension/wrapper handling rather than being cleared by staging issuer totals as positions.
gav_effect: Context only; GAV is already passing and is not used as the primary justification.
tests_validation_plan: No code changes to validate. If a future duplicate-dimension classifier change is attempted, run: pytest tests/test_bdc_cik_review.py tests/test_bdc_cik_validator.py; python -m pipeline.main --unified --validate.
residual_risk: The bundle does not include a proposed classifier patch proving these wrapper rows can be safely reclassified across filings; therefore this verdict avoids changing parser behavior and treats the case as no patch needed for this review.
reviewer_notes: The worklist reports 3 missing_from_pipeline rows totaling 171.3 million. The source-only blocker rows are position-like by name, but raw current-period source rows show the same issuer wrappers marked collapsed_duplicate_dimension_path, with examples of child rows such as Align Precision first lien loan and Class A-2 units and Centric Brands loan/equity/subordinated tranches. The XBRL/source rows remain the numeric source of truth; HTML coordinate evidence was not needed for this duplicate-dimension diagnosis.
